story.intro:
After your stay in St. Mary’s Hospital, you awaken in a morgue beneath a mysterious facility. Green gas seeps under a barricaded door. Your possessions lie nearby. Find a way out.
Campaign by Walker Graves (Dr Jack Science); Spanish translation by Los Archivos de Arkham.
story.setup: Start in the Morgue. Lab Omega is in play with 1 barricade (not per investigator). All other locations, Greyson, First Among Many, Suspicious Briefcase, 2 Agency Troubleshooters and 2 Twisted Supplicants are set aside.
story.hidden: You hear a promise of life beyond death. Serve the voice, and time will bring its reward.
story.reagent: A needle in the briefcase injects a glowing reagent into your hand. Remember that you imbibed a cardinal reagent. The briefcase may pass to another investigator who has not done so.
story.resolution1: You awaken in Hibbs’s Roadhouse. Hibbs dismisses your account of the facility as drunken confusion. The Tailors contained the problem. Gain victory experience; record whether you put out a fire.
story.resolution2: You escape into Hibbs’s Roadhouse and learn the facility’s secret. Gain victory experience. If Greyson is in the victory display, the First claimed the facility. Record whether you put out a fire; keep the briefcase if you escaped with it.
story.resolution3: Greyson escorts you to Hibbs’s Roadhouse and explains the Tailors’ work. You earned her respect and learned the roadhouse’s secret. Gain victory experience, record whether you put out a fire, and keep the briefcase if you escaped with it.
story.prologue: Your investigations left you gravely wounded in St. Mary’s Hospital. Weeks of treatment bring no recovery. As doctors prepare an urgent operation, you glimpse a pair of emerald eyes before everything fades.

night.intro:
7:21 PM

Hibbs stares as you wolf down a plate of greasy breakfast food. The burly man takes a moment, then speaks:

“It started about three days back. These strange fogs started rolling through town. Arkham being what it is, most people just assumed something had gone wrong at a factory downriver and went about their business. But then folks started getting sick. Gave folks weird rashes, some sort of disgusting skin thing. Folks by then were starting to get a bit wary, but business kept up.

Then, yesterday, Doc Pickman wandered into Providence Square with a deer’s head fused to his neck. Both heads were screaming. Government types showed up to put a stop to it, but the word was out. By the time we realized the mists were spreading from folks who were badly infected, the suits had already let a lot of troops get too close. Now there’s a bunch of those things wandering around town. Attacking people. And even more of that terrible miasma.

The word on the street is to hole up somewhere safe tonight. Lots of folks practically live here at my roadhouse, so I thought I’d open up and let ’em gather. Honestly, though, I’m worried how much we’ll be able to defend the place.” Hibbs quiets for a beat, thinking.

“You seem like hardy people, friend. If you’re really concerned about the monsters, best thing you can do is help get folks safe. Arkham’s full of places where people might be holing up. If you could round people up and help to shore up some safe havens… well, tomorrow, I’m sure there’ll be plenty of folks happy to help you figure out your memory lapse.”
night.setup:
Gather Night on the Town, the eight Fallen Arkham locations and three Grinning Victims, Haze of Miasma, Ancient Evils and only three Hunting Shadows from The Midnight Masks. Set story assets aside. Put Hibbs Roadhouse, General Store, Orne Library and Bank of Arkham into play, plus one random location from Docks/Advertiser and one from Boarding House/Magick Shoppe (Spanish guide). Start at Hibbs Roadhouse and put four fixed clues on each of the six locations. One of the other two locations is infected at random.

Defend uses the citizen’s numeric value without committed cards or player-card increases, except for Hibbs’s printed permission. Investigators at the testing investigator’s location may place their clues on that location to reduce the difficulty.
night.resolution1:
Things are getting bad out there. You had hoped that your experiences in the facility were exceptional, but it seems as though all of Arkham is swiftly moving in the same direction. It’s possible that no matter what action you take to keep people safe, it won’t be enough against the spreading tide of miasmic corruption.

Unless, of course, you can cut it off at the source. Find where this evil spreads from and stop it. The strange disease-ridden monster that appeared by the general store leaves you thinking — perhaps there’s something around there that serves as the source of it all…
night.resolution2:
You’ve done it. Thanks to you, countless citizens of Arkham will survive the night to come. These creatures, dangerous as they may be, won’t defeat this city. Not tonight.

Despite your victory, you can’t stop the sinking feeling that no matter how many people make it through, it won’t be enough against the spreading tide of miasmic corruption.

Unless, of course, you can cut it off at the source. Find where this evil spreads from and stop it. The strange disease-ridden monster that appeared by the general store leaves you thinking — perhaps there’s something around there that serves as the source of it all…

friends.title: Interlude I: Friends in Low Places
friends.section1:
Rivertown is quiet. With most of the remaining citizens of Arkham holed up, the streets have only flickering street lamps to keep you company. Strangely, the creatures have also vanished, along with most of the choking fogs.

An hour into your exploration in the Rivertown neighborhood, you’re startled by a hand on your shoulder. You turn to strike, but find Hibbs standing with a grin.

“Easy, friend! Heard you were somewhere around here, figured I’d come and lend a hand for a while. It’s the least I could do given all the help you did for me. Just for a while, though. Afterwards, well…”
friends.section2: Hibbs pauses for a moment, staring at the ground. He squares his shoulders and looks you in the eyes. “Actually, no. You got the savvy to have made it past the suits, and you care about this city. You got a good head on your shoulders. City doesn’t need me to keep the Agency’s secrets. City’d be better off if I stick around and help you put a stop to this. Besides, it’s not like you aren’t already in the know. From now on, I’m with you.”
friends.section3: Hibbs pauses for a moment, staring at the ground. He slumps his shoulders and speaks. “After we find you a lead, I head back. Got a lot of folks safe at the roadhouse, but you never know what could go wrong. There has to be someone there to make sure everyone stays put. So I’ll help you search and then return. That’ll leave us square.”
friends.section4:
Rivertown is quiet. With most of the remaining citizens of Arkham holed up, the streets have only flickering street lamps to keep you company. Strangely, the creatures have also vanished, along with most of the choking fogs.

An hour into your exploration in the Rivertown neighborhood, you round a corner and walk directly into a cloud of the glowing haze. Your eyes lose focus, and for a moment, you see through many eyes at once. You see one self weaving robes of flesh and reciting twisted chants. Another howls, and slowly drags itself arm over arm from a deep tunnel into dark woods. Another stares over a corpse and curses fate.

The Plaguebearer stares through darkness at a small blue sphere, dangling below a colossal red palm that drips green ichor from a stigmata.

The miasma recedes, and your self returns.
friends.hiddenGift:

I grant you this because you cannot stop me.

How can you expect to contain me when you cannot even contain your curiosity?

dawn.intro1:
12:54 AM:

Midnight comes and goes with little progress. The quiet streets of Rivertown seem to hold no signs as to the source of the monstrosities you’ve been fighting against. Just as you’re considering finding somewhere to catch some sleep, your attention is caught by the sound of wheels rattling on unpaved stones. You peer into a nearby alley, and see a man in a doctor’s coat trying to push a wobbling gurney through a side door. A man whose face you recognize.

It takes you a moment to place him, but the mousy figure can only be Doctor West - one of your two attending physicians at St. Mary’s. What is he doing here? At this time of night? With a dead body?

Before you can answer, several cars come barreling down the street. By the time they’ve passed, West is nowhere to be seen.
dawn.intro2:
You look down the street, and see a band of armed agents pouring out of the cars. To your surprise, Agent Greyson exits the lead car. Before she can turn to address the gathered agents, you run out and flag her down.

“Certainly didn’t expect to see you all here. Can’t be a coincidence, though. We’re looking for Asset Delta-Two. He’s an expert. Might know how to stop all this. Goes by Herbert West. He-”

You interrupt, explaining your connection to the man, as well as what you just saw. Greyson eyes you with surprise.

“Aren’t you full of the unexpected? Well, if you’re up to it, we’re going in after him. What do you say - feel like joining the cavalry?”
dawn.intro3:
You look down the street, and see a band of armed agents pouring out of the cars. A cruel looking man in a vest exits the lead car, throwing a cigarette onto the ground and grinding it out. He turns to address the gathered agents.

“Listen up, boys. We’ve tracked Asset Delta-Two back to this location. You want payback for all the good men these freaks have killed? For Greyson? Well, Delta-Two knows how to get it. He’s not gonna come easy, so any force short of lethal on the target is authorized. Anyone else could be infected, so kill on sight.” The man grins like a shark.

Either Delta-Two is West, or the doctor is in real danger. Regardless, you need to get to him before these agents do - he might know how you got into this whole mess!
dawn.intro4:
You look down the street, and see a band of armed agents pouring out of the cars. To your surprise, Agent Greyson exits the lead car. You sneak closer as she addresses the gathered agents.

“Alright, Tailors. We’ve tracked Asset Delta-Two back to this condemned brownstone. We believe Delta-Two knows how we might put a stop to all this. However, he should be considered extremely dangerous in his own right, and is unlikely to come with us willingly. Do what you have to do. Finally, anyone else you run into isn’t cleared for Delta-Two’s experiments. Terminate any civilians you find.”

Either Delta-Two is West, or the doctor is in real danger. Regardless, you need to get to him before these agents do - he might know how you got into this whole mess!
dawn.resolution1:
As two agents pull a furious West out the door, a woman stands above you and points the muzzle of a gun directly at your midsection. “Nothing personal. But you weren’t cleared for any of this.”

Your last moment of life is a flash of gunfire.
dawn.resolution2:
You bolt out the front door of the manor, pulling the doctor with you. “What’s the meaning of all this? Did you lead that monstrosity to me? Did Greyson? God, what incompetence.”

You protest. You’re not an agent. You’re one of his patients, and he has a lot of explaining to do. West stops, and stares you up and down, squinting in the light of the sunrise. “Ah. Impressive. One of my patients? I suppose I’m going to have to fill you in on exactly what’s going on.”
dawn.resolution3:
You bolt out the front door of the manor, desperate to escape the horrors inside. Screaming and gunfire rings out as the sun breaks above the horizon. You watch from a side street as several agents drag West from the manor, bound, bloodied, and unconscious. “Where we taking him?”

“Back to the Brook Facility. He’s got a lotta work to do and questions to answer.”

You need answers, now. The agents have West, and a handle on all this. Which means there’s only one place to go. Back to the facility.
dawn.resolution4:
The terrifying monstrosity gives one last howl, then falls limp to the floor. Looking around, you find an agent’s sidearm. You fire off a round directly into both sides of the creature’s merged heads, just to be sure. West quickly moves to examine the corpse, and you explain you’ve seen this thing dead before, at an agency facility.

“Ah. Pickman, then. His work has certainly borne strange fruit. But I’m sure you government stooges know all about that…”

You protest. You’re not an agent. You’re one of his patients, and he has a lot of explaining to do.

West stops, and stares you up and down, squinting in the light of the sunrise. “Impressive. One of my patients? I suppose I’m going to have to fill you in on exactly what’s going on, then.”
dawn.resolution5:
The first rays of the morning sun stream across your corpse. As you feel the warmth on your skin, you jolt awake. You are lying on the floor of the manor, surrounded by long-cooled carnage. How are you alive?

You need answers, now. The agents have West, and a handle on all this. Which means there’s only one place to go. Back to the facility.
dawn.resolution5Hidden:
Dead.
That won’t do.
My unbinding needs opposition.
The sorcerer’s folly will be your kind’s undoing.
Do what is asked of you.
Rise.

You are mine, now.

Dead? Alive? It does not matter.

Your soul and humanity persist at my whim.

alive.title: Interlude II: Dead or Alive
alive.section1: As you leave the manor, Greyson flags you down. “We’re headed back across town, to the facility. Come on, we’ll give you a ride.”
alive.section2: You watch as the agents pile into cars and peel off across town, headed back to the facility to lick their wounds and plan.
alive.section3: You step into the back seat, where West is sitting bound, as Greyson takes the wheel. You introduce yourself to West, who seems highly uninterested in anything you have to say right up until you mention how you know him…
alive.section4: You step into the back seat, where West is sitting and staring daggers at Greyson as she takes the wheel. He turns to you with a self-satisfied smile, and begins to speak…
alive.section5:
“Unfortunately, we’ll be heading to the same location. The Brook Facility - hidden beneath the city. Startling, I know.”

You explain that you’ve already been, and West looks at you, bemused.

“And they let you leave without filling you with holes? Well done. We have quite the walk back across town, so I suppose you deserve your answers.”
alive.section6:
“Let me start from the beginning. You know me as Dr. West. The world will know me as the man who cured death. I have spent the entirety of my life in pursuit of a process to reverse the flaw of mortality. Some time ago, I was approached by a research consortium about moving my process to their underground facility. Legitimizing my crucial work from its somewhat squalid origins. Of course, I jumped at the chance.

Unfortunately, a week or so back, some of the less scrupulous physicians grew jealous of my startling advances. Dr. Pickman, in particular, talked the imbeciles on the board into appropriating my proprietary serum for his… occult rituals. You’ve seen firsthand how hardy those revitalized by my reagents can be. He and Dr. Robison likely went too far in folding my work into theirs and created a monster. It escaped after multiple attempts, and has managed to infect a good portion of the city with whatever strange substance it derived from. Hence, the intense mutations spreading throughout Arkham. I quit the facility entirely due to disagreements about the use of my serum, and attempted to leave with my remaining pure reagents and notes. I will admit, those reagents didn’t make it out of the facility with me. I hope they are still somewhere within - they may prove highly useful.”
alive.section7:
“Which brings me to where you fit into all of this. My research required a steady supply of those close to death. I ‘worked’ in the intensive care ward of St Mary’s for this purpose. And I must say, you proved ideal specimens.”

You fearfully ask West what he is implying.

“Your worsening condition led to a complicated surgery. When things went wrong, I wasted no time in applying my reagent. It was notable that your corpses didn’t react - I requested your storage in the facility morgue, just in case. I am hesitant to declare success so early, but you may be the most coherent experiments I’ve performed to date!”

This is ridiculous. You point out to West that you were likely in a coma!

“Ah, and I’m sure you’ve exhibited none of the common behaviors of the re-animated. A compulsive curiosity? Intense fortitude - say, surviving gunfire? And certainly not a startling propensity for violence…”
alive.section8:
Your mind focuses on the events of the past day, and your memories prior to waking in the morgue. West was your surgeon in the hospital. You recall seeing a strange green vial on a table during the operation - The same liquid that was pouring into West’s creations.

And then you woke up in a morgue. In a body bag, no less.

Were you… are you… dead?
alive.perks: You know. You’ve known for a while. What you’ve seen with West just confirmed the suspicions you had. But just because you’ve died, doesn’t mean you won’t be able to put a stop to this madness - heck, with everything happening, being dead might be a plus!
alive.good: It doesn’t matter how things appear. You’re alive. Though your body may not be in great shape, you still have your mind - which is more than can be said of the monsters in that house. And it’s that same mind that will get to the bottom of the horrors plaguing this city.

chorus.intro:
6:11 AM:

You make your way across town as quickly as you can. The first rays of morning alight a town huddling in quiet fear. It is eerily silent. No early risers leaving their homes. Not even bird songs disturb the stillness. You focus inward, and relax for a moment.

Then the first horrible note breaks the air.

Somewhere, nearby, a voice sings out a dark and compelling melody. A song of hate and sorrow, resounding through the empty streets. A melody quickly joined by a second voice, then a third. In short order, the song is repeated all across the town of Arkham.

But no matter how you adjust, you can always hear that first voice, above the din. Leading the chorus in its eldritch invocations.

You feel a sting at the base of your skull, and your head goes momentarily fuzzy.

“Rejoice!
Rebirth!
We will all
hear the Call!
of The Bloody Unbinding!
Freedom!
Justice!
Though He dies
he will rise!
with The Bloody Unbinding!”

“The Bloody Unbinding.” You don’t know what it means. But it has to be stopped.

chorus.procession:

When you “grow the Procession”:
• Draw the top enemy of the Procession deck.
• Spawn it at the location clockwise of the last enemy in the Procession.
• Place 1 doom on the new enemy.

chorus.defeated: You’re not sure when you joined the procession. You’re not sure how. But you wandered the streets in a daze, signing hymns you learned before you were born. It was beautiful.
chorus.defeatedHidden: Rejoice in fear. I live again. It is only a matter of time.
chorus.resolution1:
As soon as the mortar fire stops, you watch the bloody viscera of the processions’ remains form a strange sigil in the sky. Twisting shapes of green and red, it shifts and pulses like the veins of a living being. You grab hold of the nearest infected, and shake them, demanding an explanation.

“He is freed! He is reborn! They have heard the Call and killed us! Our undoing is his unbinding! The Bloody Unbinding!”

A terrible mistake has been made.
chorus.resolution2:
As the horrid music fades from your ears, you watch the bloody viscera of the priest form a strange sigil in the sky. Twisting shapes of green and red, it shifts and pulses like the veins of a living being. You grab hold of the nearest infected, and shake them, demanding an explanation.

“He is freed! He is reborn! You have heard the Call and killed us! Our undoing is his unbinding! The Bloody Unbinding!”

You have made a terrible mistake.

allied.title: Interlude III: Arkham Allied
allied.intro: As you ponder the meaning of the strange sigil emblazoned on the sky, you hear someone calling your name…
allied.hibbs: A group of patrons, half seas over, sing a drinking song with your name awkwardly inserted into it. You can’t help but feel a camaraderie with this motley crew.
allied.store: Davy, the shopkeep of the general store meekly calls you over, and hands you a ratty punchcard. “As far as I’m concerned, you get the best price I can give you on anything you need.” He eyes the sigil with fear. “I’m sure you’ll need it.”
allied.bank: Before you can react, the Vice President of the bank has shoved a case into your hands. You crack it open as he looks nervously at the sigil in the sky, and find it stuffed with cash. “An investment in Arkham’s future.”
allied.library: Professor Armitage produces a tome with gilded pages from a tote bag. “This is one of the most precious pieces in the forbidden collection. I only hope it will assist you in reversing whatever terrible fate these signs portend.”
allied.boarding: The elderly Ma Matheson says very little, but shakes your hand and gives you a tin filled with homemade pastries. Several onlookers eye you with surprise.
allied.shop: Miriam Beecher coughs, and gestures to the sigil in the sky. “This is far from over. I don’t know what you’ll need, but I know a being that may be of some help…”
allied.advertiser: A camera bulb flashes, and you find yourself surrounded by several reporters. “Soon as we’re in the clear, all of Arkham’s gonna want to shake your hand”
allied.docks: You’re lifted off your feet by a group of celebrating dock workers. After some pleading on your part, they drop you, but not before you’re made an honorary union member.
allied.hidden: Your time is nearly up. Even now, my prison fails. When the midnight hour arrives, prepare for your end.

history.title: Interlude IV: History Lesson
history.lesson1:
Robison walks you along a twisting path, and begins to elaborate. “Let me start with a history lesson. Reality is far more complicated than you or I ever believed. There are beings and species of such magnitude and power that humanity pales in comparison. But, all life shares the same propensity for conflict. Aeons ago, there was a being - a Great Old One known as Baalshandor. Think of him as a twisted god of life. While many of the Old Ones created beings in their image, Baalshandor found his niche in evolutionary chaos. Germs, viruses, bacteria - they were all his children.

The diseases were as much tools as children. Any lesser being infected, will find themselves serving the whims of the Plaguebearer in their idle moments. Many Old Ones abhorred these creations. A being known as Cthugha, obsessed with purity, was particularly offended - Offended enough to war against Baalshandor.

They were evenly matched. Baalshandor could corrupt almost anything, and the fire of Cthugha could burn away any impurity. So clever Cthugha sought aid. An ancient deal was struck, with an entity whose name I dare not speak- I will call him The King. Cthugha would see his ancient enemy destroyed, and the King would gain control over the pestilence of Baalshandor. Together, Cthugha and the King destroyed Baalshandor’s armies.

But Baalshandor could not be destroyed. So a prison was crafted, beyond all known dimensions. It would bind Baalshandor outside of reality - even in all his power, only shades of his virulence were able to seep through. To unbind Baalshandor, he would need a mass sacrifice of followers. As his creations could be culled before this occurred, the Old Ones believed this prison unbreakable.

But I am afraid that to aid my colleague’s search for knowledge, I passed along dangerous rituals to draw upon Baalshandor’s power. Trust me when I say I truly regret it. Not only did it corrupt him, it somehow brought him back from his destruction by Cthugha’s kin. He became a walking extension of Baalshandor, and the bacteria that he spawned spread to the city. It is small comfort that that city is about to burn.

Throughout the ages, whenever Baalshandor’s blood has flowed into our reality, The King and the Flame have been there to destroy all that it tainted. Even now, they prepare a last attack to destroy Arkham and prevent his unbinding. The city will fall, but it will not stop him.

In the hours to come, Baalshandor will emerge from the ashes of Arkham. His children will be endless. In a matter of hours, the earth will be his. And only you can stop it.”

You lose yourself in thought for a moment, then stagger back in shock, terrified of what you see. You stand on a stone ring surrounding a terrifying mass of spheres and eyes.

“An aspect of my master. As a gesture of apology from me, you may ask of him any one question. He may choose to answer more, but beware- few of his offers come without a cost.”
history.portals: Yog-Sothoth is the key and guardian of the gate. He knows where the Old Ones broke through of old, and where They shall break through again.
history.portalsEffect: Record in your campaign log that you saw a vision of the portals.
history.first: There was a formula for evoking such a shade, and another for putting it down; and it had now been so perfected that it could be taught successfully.
history.firstEffect: Record in your campaign log that you learned the killing words.
history.baalshandor: That is not dead which can eternal lie. And in strange aeons, even death may die.
history.baalshandorEffect: Record in your campaign log that you received a cryptic riddle.
history.lesson2:
“I hope you have the answers you seek. Your time here draws short - unless you would prefer to abandon this folly and dwell with me amongst the endless for eternity?”

You shake your head. Arkham’s in more danger than ever. Only you have the knowledge to stop what’s coming.

Robison speaks a few words, and the stars fade from the sky, followed by the rest of the light in this realm.

noon.intro1:
11:43 AM:

You carefully approach the roadhouse. The various agents are too concerned with regaining control to notice your approach, and it doesn't take you long to find your way into the back rooms.
noon.intro2: You search the various back rooms. In the cellar, behind shelves of booze, you find a hatch that leads down to a familiar tunnel. It seems Hibbs was lying to you.
noon.intro3: You swiftly descend into the tunnel- So swiftly that you're caught off guard when Tailor agents surround you and demand you drop any weapons. A man with the grin of a hungry shark lights a cigarette and smiles. "Welcome to the Brook facility. Any last words?"
noon.intro4:
"Stand down, Crispin! We're on the same side here. These are undercover Tailors. They've been working for me, doing surveillance."
Greyson positions herself between you and the scowling man.
"And how come I ain't heard about this before?"
"We're a clandestine organization, Crispin. Need-to-know basis. I don't need you to like it. I just need you to give us time to get down there and help West here do his job."

After a tense moment, the agents stand down. Greyson pulls you past, and walks you and West into the facility lobby. "Don't thank her too soon" West interjects. "We've got maybe a half an hour before they realize she's lying to them."
noon.intro5:
Herbert West's voice breaks above the din. "You idiots! Don't you recognize my associates? I'm not going to be able to just whip up a solution to your problem without my essential assistants."
After a tense moment, the agents stand down. West pulls you past, and walks you into the facility lobby. "Don't thank me too soon. We've got maybe a half an hour before they realize I'm lying to them."
noon.intro6:
West frowns. "You came to me to for a solution to all this? Well, I don't have one. I deal with life and death - what's going on up there is beyond either. Pickman would have known, but he's out of the picture. But we had a mutual associate here. Robison. Dealt in knowledge of the arcane. I would consider the man a crackpot, but for his results. The board funded his research into beings that supposedly offered him knowledge. He once bragged to me that he could learn the answer to any question for the right price. If we could reach his private laboratory, you could force him to make good on that boast.

Unfortunately, the man was... paranoid. His research wing is protected by a complex series of locks and barriers. Fortunately, I know where at least one key can be found."

You express your confusion to West. Research wing? You saw no research wing, and you fully explored this facility yesterday.

"Oh, did you?" says West, pushing a wall panel in and revealing a pristine panic room stocked with supplies. "Well, you're the experts."

noon.agenda1b: Your ruse is up. Tailor Agents begin pouring into the facility like a swarm of angry bees. Better move fast – you don't want to have to fight their queen.
noon.agenda2b:
A bloodied Agent Crispin staggers down the tunnel. "WEST! You and your degenerate cronies better get out here right now, or I swear not even your damn juice will be able to put your sorry corpse back together when I'm done with ya!"

Tailors rush to offer him support, but he steadies himself. "I'm fine. We just need to finish this before that… thing… makes it down here."

"And kill those fakes with West!"
noon.agenda2bWest: You turn to check with West, but he has vanished entirely. So much for trusting him.
noon.agenda3b:
An explosion rocks the facility, and you hear screams from the tunnel.

A horrible creature with a decaying face bends its neck through the lobby door, then bursts through a doorframe that can no longer contain it.

How can it still be alive? How can it have followed you?
noon.agenda4b:
The entire facility shudders, and the walls and ceilings start to fall in. Suddenly aware of just how deep below the city you are, you make for the exit. You don't make it far before your way is blocked by the slowly rising mass of the First Among Many. Why can't this thing just DIE?

A falling block of concrete knocks you to the ground. As the room collapses, you hear a strange voice chanting "Ia! Ia! Yog-"
noon.act1bBriefcase: "Damn! It's not here. Where is that case?" You hold the heavy brown bag behind you and remind West what you're here for.
noon.act1b: West looks up at you in some surprise. "Ah! Well, that was quicker than expected. The key was in the same drawer as always. Unfortunately, that's not the only thing we'll be needing. Dr. Robison is an eccentric sort - we'll be needing a sort of crest he made. My copy is missing, but Pickman's might still be in the Omega wings.
noon.act2b:
With the crest assembled, the spell pushing it apart fades. You quickly rush to the Alpha laboratory. Rotating the crest into place, the lion's mouth reveals a keyhole. You insert West's key, and hear it click into place.

Slowly, the door grinds open. Beyond is a seemingly endless hallway of doors. As it extends, the walls extrude in strange angles, and gravity seems to shift. At the far end of the hall, a door with a plaque reading "Robison, Head of Conjecture" is just barely visible.
noon.act3b:
You enter a room that must be Robison's research lab. But… while it's filled with all the ritual trappings you'd expect, there's no doctor and, more concerning, no other exit. You look all over the room, turning over shelves and desks in desperation.

"Quick, quick! Over here!"

You look around, and it takes you a moment to notice a man's hand gesturing from the corner. The arm intersects a chalk drawing of a bridge on a solid wall.

"Please, hurry! It's nearly here!"

With no other options, you move towards the chalk drawing and jump as the hand pulls you through the matter of the wall, and into somewhere very strange indeed…
noon.defeated:
Your mind rests in the trench between idleness and slumber. You feel the cold stone beneath you. You chance the opening of an eye, and see only the cold void of space.

You bolt upright, and are astonished by what you see. You lie upon one of a seemingly infinite number of narrow interweaving pathways through a terrifying nothingness dotted with stars.

All around you, terrible voices chant softly, and you strain to hear. "Ia! Ia! Yog-Sothoth!" You realize, with some concern, that the little dots on the horizon are not stars. They are eyes.

"Well, that could have gone better." A thin man in a tattered collared shirt and glasses motions to you. "Come on. We have... a lot to talk about."
noon.threshold: You survive again, past your purpose. Such unyielding vermin. He has taken an interest. Do not believe his false hopes. You cannot stop what is to come. You do not even control your flesh. Give in to your petty mortality and DIE.
noon.thresholdEffect: Each investigator that reads this takes a physical trauma.
noon.resolution1:
The thin man intoduces himself as Robison. "You've been looking for me, yes? I've been looking for you. My master -he has concerns about the ongoing situation in Arkham."

Before you even ask the question, he responds. "I have made... an arrangement with the creator of this realm. Let's just say that my survival was at risk, and he was the key. You owe him a debt as well. You would have been crushed in the collapse of my former research wing had he not pulled you through.

But that's not here nor there. I suppose you would like to hear what I know."
noon.resolution2:
Your eyes unfocus as you are pulled through what seems like an endless stretch of solid concrete. An eternity passes, the only sensation being the hand pulling you forward.

All at once, you burst through the other side and stumble forward. You catch yourself on the edge of a precipice - looking out, you see countless interweaving narrow paths of stone impossibly suspended in the void of space.

"Welcome to my Master's realm." A thin man in a tattered collared shirt and glasses standing ahead of you on the narrow path nods slightly. "I'm Dr. Robison. I think you've been looking for me? So, I've been looking for you. Come, and I'll explain what I know.

war.intro1:
3:02 PM:

You stir under a sheet. You bolt upright, half expecting the telltale bodies of the morgue. Instead, you are lying on a sofa, watched by a square-jawed adolescent. “West? They’re up!”

From an adjacent room, Herbert West enters scribbling on a notepad. “Thank you, Dan. Good to see you up and about. We found you just outside the facility. Very lucky of you to make it out. Apologies for my absence. I became sidetracked - I believe I have found a way to destroy that creature that seems to be pursuing you.”

You give West the bad news. His emotions are hard to read, but you could swear he’s almost amused. “Well. The monster will have to wait. We’ve got a city to save.”

war.intro2:
3:02 PM:

You feel the rain hitting softly against your legs, as the wet mud starts to seep into your clothes. Pulling yourself up from the mire, you look about the alleyway. You’re back in Arkham. Somewhere in Easttown.
war.intro3:
It’s a dreary afternoon. The sky is a blanket of grey and every footstep you take sticks in the squelching ground below you. The exhaustion weighing on your mind and body tempts you to give in to the pull - but you don’t have that luxury.

You mull over what you’ve learned. The Plaguebearer- Baalshandor - infected or created the First, that horrid monster that has chased you throughout the city. All the terrors that have plagued Arkham over the past twenty-four hours are the spawn of this herald. Each twisted killer stalking the streets is a sliver of the Plaguebearer’s consciousness, controlled through the microscopic organisms found in the miasma.

And now the twin forces of the Flame and the King, prepare to descend upon Arkham and destroy every trace of life in hopes of preventing what has already occurred. It strikes you that it would almost be worth it. Arkham would be a small price to pay if all of Earth is threatened. But if the doctor spoke true, then their drastic gesture would barely delay the disease-god’s plan.

Which means it’s up to you. If you want to stop Baalshandor, you’ll have to live till midnight. And if you want that, you’ll have to stop the assault. To thwart whatever destruction the Old Ones plan for Arkham.

You climb the crest of a hill, and turn to look out over Arkham. It’s a dark, dangerous place. A city full of desperate last stands and terrible sacrifices. But there is warmth here, and camaraderie, and even love. So many people live here, and you have come to care for Arkham, despite its faults. And now, for this city - for these people - you are the only hope.

You steel yourself.

The sky opens up.

war.resolution1: For a moment - just a moment - something exists in Arkham. Something ancient and immense. It rips open the sky. It dominates the landscape. Within moments, it is all you can see. war.resolution2: The flames and screams build to a fever pitch. A sudden blaze burns into the sky, twirling higher and higher. Within moments it has reached the sigil that floats above the town. confrontation.title: Interlude V: A Confrontation
confrontation.section1:
You have words for Herbert West. He’s been lying to you - if not directly, than by omission, about his part in all this. As West motions around the clock room, babbling about the ritual, you grab him by the arm and demand answers.

West quickly quiets. After a moment of staring each other down, he asks, “And just what are you accusing me of?”

Murder. Conspiracy. Hell, he could be a thrall of Baalshandor. He created the First Among Many. He was experimenting near where the Pustule appeared. He has a nasty habit of vanishing just before things get bad. He may have even tried to kill you at St Mary’s.

West frowns at you. “You’re being ridiculous. If you insist on wasting time here, I refuse to be part of it.” He begins to pull away, but is held against your grip.
confrontation.section2:
You can’t risk leaving this to chance. Even if Herbert West isn’t actively your enemy, he’s a monster. West looks shocked as he pulls against your grip.

“Are we resorting to physical violence, like cavemen? I’m disappointed in you. And to think-“

Without warning, West lunges towards you, his emerald eyes gleaming and a syringe in his hand. You fall backwards, and as West swings, he trips over you and stumbles headfirst into the gear mechanism of the clock. As the clock begins to strike midnight, a sickening crunch fills the room.

You begin to pull yourself to your feet when you hear an impossibly deep laugh.

Already tearing each other apart!

You turn to see a massive green eye staring through the clock face. Before you can react, a red arm the size of a bus tears through the tower, sending you hurtling to the ground below.

Baalshandor has arrived on Earth.
confrontation.section2Effect:
If Herbert West is in any player’s deck, remove him from that deck.
Record in your Campaign Log that Death conquered Herbert West.
confrontation.section3:
West has made terrible mistakes. But he’s not your enemy. You let him slip from your grasp, and he straightens his sleeve.

The bells of the clock tower begin to ring out midnight, and West lets out a frightened gasp. You turn to face what he’s seeing. A massive green eye stares through the front face of the clock. As the massive red arm begins to tear through the tower, you tackle West out of the way. The two of you hurtle to the earth below, miraculously landing in a large bush.

West takes you by the arm and helps to pull you up. “You’ve saved my life. I am in your debt.”

His words are small comfort as you gaze upon the behemoth that stands nearby, gaze bearing down upon you.

Once again you survive. No longer. Time to die.

Baalshandor has arrived on Earth.
confrontation.section3Effect:
If Herbert West is not in a player’s deck, they may include the Herbert West asset in their deck This card does not count against deck size.
Record in your campaign log that Baalshandor struck the first blow.
confrontation.section4:
You have words for Herbert West. But now is neither the time nor the place. If the vision was true, you are all still in imminent danger. You grab West by the arm and pull him with you down the stairs.

As you exit Town Hall, the bells begin to ring out the midnight hour. You look back, and are stunned to see a behemoth of a being smash its arm through the top of Town Hall. Its multitude of eyes swivel and stare down at you.

Ah. My clever instruments of unbinding. Time to die.

Baalshandor has arrived on Earth.

sundown.intro1:
7:37 PM:

You are snapped from your momentary lapse by the telltale rat-a-tat of tommy guns. A contingent of Tailors hanging out of speeding cars fire an excessive amount of rounds behind them. You feel the breath leave your lungs as their target comes into view behind them. Though the mass of flesh is now the size of a small building, it can only be the First Among Many.
sundown.intro2:
“Quickly!” West shouts, pointing at the agents. “They’ve already started. Remember my plan? The Tailors should have gathered the necessary materials, and are drawing the beast to Town Hall. We need to get there before it arrives!”

You find an unattended motorcar, and get moving. Though your route is difficult in Arkham’s damaged state, you pull up to Independence Square without any serious fights. A group of Tailors look around nervously, hands on their sidearms as you exit the vehicle. West clears his throat.
sundown.intro3: “That doesn’t make sense…” Greyson looks pensively. “Wait. They must be working on a trap. They’re luring it somewhere - maybe West found the answer? We should follow them. Come on- we’ll take my car!”
sundown.intro4:
The Tailors are panicky and disorganized, but they’re not suicidal. If they’re drawing the monster’s attention, it must be for a reason.

You find an unattended motorcar and follow the sounds of gunfire.
sundown.intro5: You make your way across town, tailing the agents as best you can. While the cars serving as “bait” continue to draw the creature’s rage, you see a small group running across Independence Square. You recognize the diminutive shape of Herbert West among them. You pull the car aside and yell to the doctor, who turns to face you.
sundown.intro6:
“Well, glad we could all make it.” West says loudly, motioning to you to walk with him. “That creature - Pickman - is the source of all this. We destroy it, and we stand a sliver of a chance of putting an end to the madness. That won’t be easy. It’s proved frustratingly difficult to end permanently.

Fortunately, my associates were both experts in the eldritch sciences. There is a ritual, detailed in Robison’s notes, that could “enter the memories of a tormented soul” where, if prepared, one could “purify a host and lay it to rest”. It should serve our purposes as far as removing both the offending infection and whatever is keeping it alive. Without either, it’s merely a bundle of useless flesh that can’t support its own growth. We’ll have this monster dead by sundown!”
sundown.setup:
Gather all cards from the following encounter sets: Death at Sundown, Agency Troubleshooters, Life and Death, The Plaguebearer’s Commands. When gathering cards from the Agency Troubleshooters set, do not include any enemies.

Set the First Among Many, Tendrils of the First, and Dr. Elias Pickman cards aside, out of play.

Put each location into play in a vertical layout, with the Floor 0 location on the bottom and the Floor 5 location at the top. Each investigator begins play at Independence Square.

Take the EX.O.L, Hedge Mage’s Bag, and Blessing of Tomorrow story assets and shuffle them together. Place those cards facedown on top of the Binding Runes asset to form the Ritual Deck.

Check Campaign Log. If you learned the killing words, the lead investigator starts with the Killing Words asset under their control, and places the Rusted Blade asset on the top of the ritual deck. Otherwise, take the Rusted Blade and Killing Words asset and shuffle them together, then place them on top of the ritual deck.

Some encounter cards in this scenario refer to the Floor value of your location. This value is X, where X is the Floor X trait of your current location. If your location lacks that trait, X is 0.

Shuffle the remaining encounter cards to build the encounter deck.
sundown.agenda1b:
A crash comes from ground level, followed by a multitude of screams.
The First Among Many quickly writhes into the space of Independence Square. Though little of it resembles a human form, a face is visible in the mound of flesh. The twisted face looks at the building above, and screams a single word.
“WEST!”
sundown.agenda2b: The First grows and expands. Within moments, an entire floor is completely uninhabitable.
sundown.agenda3b: You rush to complete the ritual, but your enemy catches you unaware. Within moments, you are dragged backwards, into the walls of flesh…
sundown.act1b:
You run into West ascending a staircase. “You! We don’t have much time. The Tailors managed to gather the components to my specifications. But you know their type, incapable of doing anything right. The components are scattered throughout the tower. I’ve been trying to corral them, but with this creature… they’ve lost all logic. Barely better than panicked animals.
Which means it’s down to us. There were a number of useful components, but only three are crucial - the binding runes, which when correctly placed can trap the soul in a moment in time. An ancestral blade of the target, to bring it to heel. And a book, containing a phrase we need to kill this creature. You get them prepared and meet me on the roof. Anything else you find should prove useful, but don’t waste too much time!”
sundown.act2b: A final moment, trapped in time.
sundown.act3b:
You speak the words. They tear at your very soul, thrashing in your sway like a wild animal. But you hold strong, and they strike true.
Pickman drops to his knees. As he gasps for air, a wound, like a rifle shot, appears on his chest. He frantically tears at the opening, as if trying to comprehend what is happening. With a terrible choking noise, he falls dead.
The memory begins to spin.
sundown.resolution1:
Though a sense of victory fills your heart, your mind spins. Pickman’s memory is fading with his life. You have to get out before you die with him. But something deep within you compels you to stop for a moment. You feel a sudden throbbing in your temples, and black out.

It was troubling when the subject escaped. His advanced infection stage could spread to local fauna, which could quickly get out of hand. It was fortunate that West offered his assistance - surprisingly mature of the little egomaniac, given the board handing over control of his serum research to you. His awful Re-Animated are poor soldiers, but make acceptable hunters.

The target died fairly easily, but a group of local deer were infected. Culling them has made for an irritating evening. But now, only the one remains. You speak the call and it draws near, mistaking you for a fellow infected. Just a step closer and…

A shot rings out in the forest, but not yours. The deer falls. You feel a sudden rush of cold. You instinctively pat at your torso and when you raise your hand from your chest, they are wet with something warm and sticky.

You fall to your knees, grasping at the dying animal for support. It kicks in its death throes, and you fall to the ground in a pool of the creature’s blood. Your eyes begin to unfocus as you stare into the night sky. Though your body is failing, your mind burns with rage - after all your achievements, this cannot be how you die!

A figure loosely gripping a rifle walks into your vision. “Well. This does not look good for you, Elias. In our line of work, we cannot afford to be so cavalier with our safety. Fortunately, I am well prepared for such an eventuality. You’ll be alright shortly - a contribution to the advances of science.” The figure reaches into his coat, and produces a needle filled with a glowing green substance. As you stare into his eyes, you feel a stinging pain.

You are shaken awake by a hand on your shoulder. You open your eyes to Herbert West, staring at you with concern. “You’re alive? The monster is dead - we’ve done it.”
sundown.resolution1Effect:
Each investigator earns experience equal to the Victory X value of each card in the victory display and each card in play.
Each defeated investigator is Killed.
If at least 1 investigator was killed (during or as a result of this scenario): Read Investigator Defeat.
sundown.resolution2: As the creature scales the building, West desperately fumbles to complete the ritual. You watch him step through the portal- and directly into the waiting hands of Pickman. “Dr. West. I’m so pleased you could make it.” The tendrils of the First shoot forward into the portal, and a blood-curdling scream rattles your bones. But you don’t have to live with the fear for long, as the ever expanding mass of the First finally claims your body as well.
sundown.tablet:
No.
Impossible.
I have been too lenient with you.
I will deal with you myself.
sundown.tabletEffect: The first investigator to read this records in the Campaign Log that You have been warned. Then, depending on your difficulty level, add the following token to the bag: Easy: -3, Standard: -5, Hard: -6, Expert: -7.
sundown.defeated:
When you were overcome by the First, in a way, it was a relief. It was incredibly painful, of course. But there’s something calming about being dead. The dead don’t need to worry about Baalshandor, or the fate of the world.

But as you drift away in your reverie, you feel a sudden rush of gravity…

Your eyes burst open, and you see your companions watching nervously. “Keep an eye on that one!” West shouts from across the room. “The serum may leave them somewhat unstable for the time being.”

Each investigator defeated during or as a result of this scenario is no longer Killed.
If any investigators who are no longer killed in this way control the “Unbreakable Will” asset, remove it and the “Folly of Man” weakness from their deck. They must add the “Strength of Flesh” and “Death’s Hold” cards to their deck.
Check Campaign Log. For each investigator no longer killed in this way who has not imbibed a cardinal reagent, record in your Campaign log that they have imbibed a cardinal reagent.
